parsed.why: National seat: no local bathroom ban of its own and placed on the July 2026 low-risk list, but the nationally attached facilities restriction operates directly and is unrepealable locally, and its protective reputation is expressly unsettled. Modestly above the parent average.

Statutory gender-identity nondiscrimination covering public accommodations, hate-crime coverage, repealed panic defence, gender-neutral single-user bathrooms, and 2023-24 shield laws protecting travelling trans people. No local bathroom ban. Clearly the strongest division, well above the national line.

Broad statutory gender-identity protections including public accommodations, hate-crime coverage, repealed panic defence, accessible X markers; restrictions confined to students and athletics, assessed as unlikely to reach adults. Slightly below the shielded jurisdiction.

Adult-reaching bathroom ban in government buildings enforced via a public complaint-reporting form, with a documentary defence no visitor can satisfy; $500/day flag fines and no public-accommodations protection. Tier-1 universal exposure, below the parent.

Bathroom ban extended to public colleges and universities in May 2026, no hate-crime statute, unrepealed sodomy, prison treatment freeze; but courts have stayed enforcement and no complaint-reporting machinery exists, leaving it just above dossier 4.
